text:
Certainly wild to see $KRKNF under $3/share.

In August I wrote about my frustrations and that there were better opportunities than waiting for the Anduril ramp, which was clearly delayed. Sentiment has only dragged lower since.

But there's a lot of factors.

1) The market completely turned on drones. I think it's because a massive premium to defense stocks and they ran ahead of the story which is in reality a multi-year buildout. While AI stocks accelerated fundamentals, drone stocks serve Governments, with lumpy earnings and contract awards that move at a slow pace. Unlike software names that fell out of favor for a few months, you can't argue any of these defense stocks are extremely undervalued by PE, FCF etc. $KRKNF is down 14% in a year while 
$AVAV
 and 
$KTOS
 are down 60%. Even over the last month, all my strategies gained except my defense picks down 6%... it just feels never ending. Feels like it was a hot theme and the market is over it.

2) I wrote that Anduril's ramp looks to be delayed by a year at least, muddying the explosive short term revenue thesis on Kraken, which I feel needs to see a U.S. battery facility and a Navy order to confirm. Sometimes I think Anduril gets a little too much smoke blown up them when they are still very unproven and have a long ways to go to actually scale orders to billions. Feels like the underwater division is just waiting for a U.S. Navy order that is taking longer than expected, with testing across the Dive-XL and Dive LD. I didn't see anything in the defense budget that indicated a large order in FY27 for subsea drones.

3) There's no uplisting. I thought surely Kraken would be off a junior exchange by now and definitley should be on the NASDAQ and I have no idea why it has not. Institutions don't own enough of the stock, and it just doesn't have volume to move.

Overall, probably some more love for the stock on the back half of the year from earnings which is where they do most of their revenue. Just in a really nasty trap here where investors are frustrated, stock is falling, the catalyst is delayed, and there's more exciting, fast moving sectors of the market like AI to invest in.

Since 2023-2024 you could buy anything with AI in the deck and it went up with everything else.

This summer was different. Half of the ten biggest tech names were up and the other half were down, and Nasdaq multiples have compressed about 20% this year with the 10-year above 5.25%.

That is what a maturing cycle looks like. 

When multiples stop expanding, earnings have to do the work, and earnings are where this trade is strongest this Q. 
$MU
 just guided to $61.5B for a single quarter, lead times across the supply chain are still stretching, and semis trade at a discount to the S&P.

A market that moves together rewards being early, and we've had plenty of that over the last year.But that phase is mostly gone. 

A market that splits apart rewards knowing where the bottleneck is, layer by layer, and which companies get paid when it tightens. 

Not all companies are created equal, and we are seeing big dispersion between them.

A year ago the easy money was just owning the right theme. Now it goes to the right companies within each theme, and to knowing what sets them apart.
